text: Thyroid medication is usually taken the same way every day, on an empty stomach with water, and 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast.

source.title: American Thyroid Association — Taking thyroid medication

text: Coffee taken at the same time can reduce absorption of levothyroxine; wait 30 to 60 minutes.

source.title: Levothyroxine food and drink interaction review

text: Calcium, iron supplements and antacids should be separated from the dose by about 4 hours.

source.title: American Thyroid Association — Thyroid medication interactions

text: Soy and very high-fiber foods may reduce absorption if taken together with the dose; keep timing consistent.

source.title: American Thyroid Association — Thyroid medication and food

text: Biotin supplements can distort thyroid blood tests; ask the doctor whether to pause before a test.

source.title: American Thyroid Association — Thyroid function tests

text: Avoid high-dose iodine and kelp supplements; both too little and too much iodine can affect the thyroid.

source.title: American Thyroid Association — Iodine and thyroid disease

text: Selenium: the evidence is mixed; no high-dose supplements without a doctor.

source.title: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Selenium

text: A gluten-free diet has no evidence of reducing symptoms in autoimmune thyroid disease, and the lab-value evidence is small and weak. It is needed only for coeliac disease.

source.title: American Academy of Family Physicians — Gluten-free diets and thyroid disease
